thread:
anika: RFC follow-up — proposing we extract tenant routing + enrichment into a lightweight 'softbound' service. Goal: reduce hotpath surface area and make ownership obvious, but keep rollback/fallback trivial. Phased cutover per tenant cohort. Looking for tradeoffs and safety ideas.

miles: curious about data ownership — will enrichment writes move to the new service or stay in monolith with an RPC shim?

anika: plan A is ownership move: enrichment service becomes the source-of-truth for enrichment state; plan B is read/write shim that proxies to monolith for writes (safer). Leaning toward plan B for phase 1 to avoid big DB migrations.

hiro: +1 to phase 1 shim. We should define a minimal contract so both sides can validate. Example contract: 
```json
{
  "GET /v1/tenant/{id}/enrichment": { "response": { "features": ["string"] } },
  "POST /v1/tenant/{id}/enrichment": { "payload": { "patch": {"type": "object"} } }
}
```
Keep payload tiny — no heavy joins.

tara: observability notes: we need per-tenant latency and error percentiles, plus a histogram for enrichment compute time. Also tie eval quality metrics to the rollout cohort so we can detect regression in prompt outputs. Suggest adding a synthetic tenant test that runs every minute during the canary.

miles: operational safety: can we implement a 'transparent fallback' header? e.g., new-service returns X-Fallback:monolith when it proxied. That allows tracing and easy rollback. Also add a gateway-level short-circuit that routes 100% back to monolith on rule flip.

hiro: implementation idea — deploy the enrichment service behind a facade that implements the exact monolith HTTP surface. Steps: 1) shim route -> new service; 2) feature flag per-tenant; 3) incremental traffic shift by cohort; 4) if error rate > threshold, flip back globally for that cohort. Keep a hybrid read path initially: reads from new service, writes proxied to monolith. After cohorts are healthy, flip writes to new service and drain.

anika: KV cache ownership question — currently monolith owns the prefix cache. We should either: a) move the cache to the new service (adds warmup complexity), or b) keep cache in monolith and add a cache-read API the new service calls. Preference B for phase 1 since it avoids widespread cache invalidation. Documenting this as a tech-debt ticket to fully migrate later.

tara: metrics + runbook: define SLO windows (p50/p95 latency target), and alerting thresholds: errors > 0.5% for 5m or latency p95 > 2x baseline for 10m. On alert, runbook should: check X-Fallback header rates, flip cohort flag, open incident channel, and enable detailed tracing.

miles: one more risk — migration atomicity for tenant config changes. If monolith and new service read/write different schema versions, we need compatibility layer. Suggest adding a compatibility test harness in CI that runs both codepaths for a suite of mutations.

deploy-bot: canary policy created: cohorts=[5% random tenants, 10% next wave], monitoring hooks: enrichment.latency, enrichment.errors, enrichment.fallback_ratio. Canary window: 60m.

anika: timeline & owners: phase 1 (shim + facade + cohort flag + basic metrics) = 3 sprints (owner: anika). Phase 2 (write cutover + cache move + DB migration planning) = 2–3 sprints (owner: hiro). Tech debt paydown ticket created for full cache migration and contract hardening.

hiro: happy to own phase 2 planning. I'll draft migration checklist: data model compatibility checks, draining plan, backfill script pattern, and warmup strategy for cache.

tara: I'll pair on the synthetic test harness and add evaluation hooks. Also adding a dashboard template to Console so PMs can monitor quality regressions per cohort.

anika: thanks — I'll open the RFC PR with the shim + minimal contract and tag @miles @hiro @tara for review. Can someone volunteer to pair on the cutover dry-run (staging)?

miles: I can pair next Tue. :+1:

anika: perfect — will add to the PR. :rocket:
